prior_review_correction_acknowledgement: My prior review's critical_issue on S04 was WRONG. I asserted that picks do not write manufacturing_ingredient_consumption events and therefore would not block MO delete. That was incorrect. Verified in this re-review: pickManufacturingIngredientInTx at lib/inventory/kernel/operations/manufacturing.ts:319 writes inventoryEvents with eventType='manufacturing_ingredient_consumption' at lines 388 and 412 (subtype 'manufacturing_pick'). The MO delete guard at app/(dashboard)/manufacturing/queries.ts:6446-6500 filters by eventType only (no subtype discrimination). Therefore picks DO block MO delete. S04's stuck-stale-after-pick premise is correct. I retract the prior CI on S04 and apologize for the misdirection — the revised S04 in scenarios.json properly retains the picks-block-cancel premise and cites the verification evidence in its evidence[] block.

production_bug_discovery_integrity.claim_in_scenarios_json: validateSalesLineLinkInTx at app/(dashboard)/manufacturing/queries.ts:729-819 does NOT check for an existing_active_mo on the link target; BR-1's one-time-claim invariant is enforced only by the bulk-from-SO preview filter; PUT/edit-add-link bypasses it (S29).
production_bug_discovery_integrity.verification_method: Read of queries.ts:729-819. Function signature accepts (tx, values, existingSnapshot?). Body checks: (a) both ids present or both null (lines 738-748); (b) line.deletedAt IS NULL AND line.orderStatus === 'open' AND line.itemId === values.productId (lines 774-786, returns snapshot); (c) same-snapshot rebind fallback when isUnchangedSnapshot is true (lines 788-812). There is NO SELECT against manufacturingOrders for an existing claim with the same salesOrderLineId. The only enforcement of BR-1 is lib/manufacturing/sales-order-manufacturability.ts:222-235 (existing_active_mo skip reason in the bulk preview), which is bypassed entirely by the single-create POST and the edit-PUT paths.
production_bug_discovery_integrity.conclusion: Production bug discovery is CONFIRMED. The defect is genuine, high-severity (data corruption risk: any user with module:manufacturing write can multiply-claim a sales line via the edit path), and well-localized. S15, S24, and S29 each pin a different facet of the gap. The suggested fix in production_bug_discovery.suggested_fix is correct in form (add the existing_active_mo check before returning the snapshot, gate on isUnchangedSnapshot to avoid blocking self-rebinding).
production_bug_discovery_integrity.phase_4_action_required: When S29 fails with PUT returning 200 + two MOs claiming the same line, Phase 4 should: (a) open a Linear issue against the ERP team for the BR-1 PUT-path violation, (b) attach scenarios-review.json and the failing test output as evidence, (c) propose the suggested fix from production_bug_discovery.suggested_fix. The test should be checked in as-is (asserting the BR-1 violation) so the Linear fix PR will flip it to assert PUT returns 409. Until the fix lands, this test documents the current production contract.

s04b_testability.trigger_concreteness: Concrete but multi-step. Setup matches S04's path through MO_WORK_STARTED but uses different-itemId SO rewrite. Trigger sequence: (1) finish picking all remaining ingredients via POST /api/manufacturing-orders/[mo]/ingredients/[ing]/pick (with Idempotency-Keys per BR-8a), (2) POST /api/manufacturing-orders/[mo]/complete with Idempotency-Key, (3) attempt SO DELETE → 400 BR-6, (4) attempt MO DELETE → 400 production-output, (5) re-attempt both → both stable. The completion endpoint requires all ingredients picked first (verified at app/api/manufacturing-orders/[id]/complete/route.ts:12-31), which the scenario correctly handles in the trigger sequence. Phase 4 must implement step (1) as a loop over all ingredients, not a single call. The scenario is reachable but slow lane is correct.

no_duplicate_scenarios.rationale: S12 covers BR-5 item-side bulk delete (product/material referenced by open MO). S21 covers BR-5 MO-side bulk delete (clean MO + finalized MO in same batch). Different deletion targets, different guards (deleteItem vs deleteManufacturingOrdersInTx). Both pin atomic-fail invariant on different surfaces.

T26 is the state-model transition for 'item-delete when only done MOs reference it'. S25 covers the symmetric case (item-delete when only cancelled MOs reference it, deletedAt SET). The state-model T26 captures done-only; S25 captures cancelled-only — both filter on deletedAt IS NULL but with different MO terminal states.

S04 covers RA-2c stuck-stale at MO_WORK_STARTED (picks block cancel; T18b explicitly out of scope). S04b covers T18b: complete the stuck MO to reach MO_DONE (production output blocks cancel for a different reason). Different terminal states, different finalized-guard branches, different recovery paths (none for S04b — permanently terminal).

S11 covers BR-6 first branch (stale salesOrderLineId pointing outside SO's current lines, after different-itemId rewrite). S23 covers BR-6 second branch (linked MO has active allocation pointing to a different SO's line). Different guard code paths inside deleteSalesLinkedManufacturingOrdersInTx (the stale-line guard at 2367-2375 vs the cross-SO allocation guard at 2378-2397).

S15 covers homogeneous parallel single-create + single-create (both POST /api/manufacturing-orders, neither acquires FOR UPDATE on salesOrders). S24 covers heterogeneous parallel bulk + single (bulk acquires FOR UPDATE on salesOrders, single does not — cross-endpoint race the state-model flagged as 'no_guard_exists: true'). Both pin BR-1 enforcement but on different concurrency surfaces.

S15 covers BR-1 violation via parallel single-create POST (two concurrent POSTs claim same line). S29 covers BR-1 violation via PUT/edit-add-link (existing unlinked MO PUT-ed onto a claimed line). Different code paths, different trigger sequences, different root causes (concurrency vs validation-gap). Both pin the production defect from different angles.

S26 covers parallel PUT + DELETE on same MO (concurrency, two distinct operations contending). S27 covers PUT + PUT on same MO (sequential retries, same operation, asserts natural idempotency). Different bug classes (data corruption vs duplicate-write).

S03 covers single-line SO edit + MO snapshot rebind via isUnchangedSnapshot fallback. S28 covers many-to-many same-itemId rewrite where moveReplacedSalesLineAllocationsInTx must pair allocations by itemId+sortOrder. Different functions, different observables (MO snapshot vs stockAllocations migration).
